_about: Neon Glow v1 (trained 5 Oct 2026 from 5 Top-100 refs: #15 snippco r23, #21 raw.to.reel r37, #44 drive r33, #52 jim.malingin, #83 marvin.media; ~/reels/style-train/neon-glow). Punchy UGC talking head in natural colour on a dark or neutral set: bold white sans captions at chest height, ONE keyword per line in a glowing neon colour (green by default; serif italic with a soft glow), neon icon/emoji pops beside the head, red strike-through on dismissed claims, a red-X list for 'not this', and a short white light-leak flash over a take join. Busy picture (a change every ~1.5-2 s), light upbeat electronic bed. | 6 Oct lead: layout.cardY 230 kept for readability (fixes caption/list collision; scored 56.4 vs 60.5, readability wins).

director.style: Neon Glow: a punchy UGC talking head. The speaker stays in natural colour (no B&W, no film look); the energy comes from captions where one word per line glows in a neon colour, small neon icons that pop beside the head on the nouns, and fast punch-ins.
director.captions: captions.highlight: ONE keyword per 3-word line at most, and only content words (the noun, number or verb that carries the claim; never 'the', 'so', 'cause', 'really'). About one glowing keyword every 2-3 s. Lowercase white bold for everything else.
director.icons: emoji or logo beats (neon-looking: money, question mark, warning, check, cross, the product's simple-icons slug) on the 2-4 most concrete nouns, 1.0-1.6 s each, never two at once. Brand names -> logo; feelings/ideas -> emoji.
director.cards: strike beat on a claim the speaker dismisses ('not X', a myth). list beat ONLY for 'not this' lists with stampAt (red-X look): without a stamp the engine still draws strike lines, so a positive enumeration should use icon beats or captions.highlight instead. At most one big beat (count) for a number or a price.
director.transitions: Hard cuts. One white light-leak flash (leaks) over a take join every ~8 s; no glitch, no wipes.
director.rhythm: Picture changes every ~1.5-2 s (punch-ins via cadence, icon pops, cards). Leave the first 0.5 s clean on the speaker's face.
